meta.title: For Guests
meta.description: What to expect when you visit the Burnaby Entrepreneurs Toastmasters Club — meeting flow, cost, and why entrepreneurs specifically get value from Toastmasters.

page_hero.headline: Come see a meeting.
page_hero.intro: Wednesdays, 6:00 – 8:00 pm at Metropolis at Metrotown. Visiting is free — no membership, no commitment, and you will not have to speak in front of the room.

club_experience.heading: What does the club experience offer?

items.text: Feedback and evaluations in a supportive environment
An opportunity to take on club leadership positions
The ability to assume club meeting roles
Practice giving prepared and impromptu speeches

why.headline: A surprising number of business problems are communication problems in a strategy costume.
paragraphs: The pitch didn't land. The team left the meeting with three different interpretations. The great hire went elsewhere because someone else told a better story. The conference invite came and you said no.
Toastmasters is a weekly, low-stakes place to practise the things that are high-stakes everywhere else — and to hear honest feedback from people who have no reason to flatter you.

situations.heading: Mapped to the business you're building

rows.drill: Prepared speeches teach you to open hard, structure an argument, and land a close in a fixed time — with a timer running, exactly like a real pitch.
Table Topics (impromptu speaking) is 1–2 minutes of thinking on your feet in front of an audience. It is the closest simulation of an unexpected question there is.
Every meeting is member-run. You will chair, keep time, and move an agenda — skills nobody teaches and everyone is judged on.
Evaluation trains you to give specific, useful, non-crushing feedback. That single skill changes how a team performs.
Vocal variety, gesture, and pacing are separate trainable projects, not vague talent.
A room of ~20 Burnaby-area entrepreneurs who see you every week. Repeated exposure beats a hundred cold coffee chats.

quotes.body: Being in Toastmasters pushes you to take on challenges that you wouldn't have taken on by yourself. You start stepping up more for a project and want to take on more responsibility and become a leader.
The training has made me more focused and disciplined at work and improved my interactions with colleagues.
quotes.attribution: Adrian Jefferson Chofor, Marketing Operations Consultant, Kaiser Permanente

agenda.heading: Start to finish — so you can picture the whole thing before you arrive.

items.text: Meeting begins. The Toastmaster of the evening (a member, rotating each week) welcomes everyone and introduces guests by name. You'll be asked to wave or say hello — that's it.

Prepared speeches and evaluations. Two or three members deliver 5–7 minute speeches from their Pathways projects — each one working on a specific skill like persuasion, vocal variety, or storytelling.

Table Topics and evaluations. Members and guests are called at random to give a 1–2 minute impromptu answer to a question. Guests may be invited but can pass with zero awkwardness. This is the fun part and the part that makes people join.
Reports and awards. The timer, the grammarian, and the ah-counter report back. Best Speaker and Best Table Topics are voted on.
Guest feedback. We ask what you thought. Say anything, including 'not for me' — nobody chases you.
Close. Some members head out for dinner afterwards.

agenda.promise: You will not speak in front of the audience if you do not want to.

pathways.headline: Toastmasters isn't an open-mic night.
pathways.intro: Members work through Pathways, the organisation's structured education programme, so every speech has a specific skill objective and a rubric behind it.
how_items: Take a short online assessment when you join; it suggests a learning path based on your goals.
Choose from six paths. New members receive one path free.
Each path has five levels — fundamentals first, then increasingly demanding projects.
You progress by delivering speeches at club meetings and applying the feedback. Entirely self-paced.
Over 300 practical workplace skills are covered across the programme, available online and in multiple languages.

cost.headline: Visiting is free and always will be.
cost.footer: For context: a single day of corporate presentation-skills training typically runs into four figures. This is roughly the price of a monthly streaming bundle, and it runs every week, forever.

closing.headline: The next meeting is this Wednesday.
closing.body: 6:00 pm, Winners Community Room at Metropolis at Metrotown — through the two double doors beside Winners. Come at 5:45 and we'll introduce you around. No RSVP required, but it's nice to know you're coming.
